newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-DITKA TO COACH SAINTS, PAPER SAYS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-DITKA TO COACH SAINTS, PAPER SAYS.

text.p: Mike Ditka, who coached the Chicago Bears to their only Super Bowl victory after the 1985 season, will coach the New Orleans Saints, a Chicago newspaper reported on Monday.
"I'm going to climb the mountain one more time," Ditka said in Monday's Chicago Sun-Times. "I might fall on my (butt), but it's going to be done."
The Saints are expected to officially name Ditka on Tuesday.
The Chicago Sun-Times said Ditka has already started to assemble a staff and that former Bears assistants Danny Abramowicz and Zaven Yaralian are among those hired.
Ditka, who was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 1988, has served as an NFL broadcaster for NBC Sports.
Ditka coached the Bears from 1982-92, compiling a 112-68 record, including a 6-6 record in the post-season.

Aside from the strike-shortened 1982 season, Ditka had only two losing seasons (1989, 1992) and had seven seasons of at least 10 wins. Ditka won six NFC Central titles and advanced to three NFC Championship games.
In 1985, the Bears went 15-1 in theregular season, losing only to Miami after a 12-0 start. Chicago advanced to Super Bowl XXI in New Orleans, where it pummeled the New England Patriots, 46-10.

The fiery former tight end was named Coach of the Year in 1988, posting a 12-4 record despite a mid-season heart attack. He holds the NFL record for most wins in a four-year span with 52, done from 1985-88.

He was named the NFL Rookie of the Year in 1961, following a season in which he caught 56 passes as a tight end. He appeared in the Pro Bowl in all six seasons he was with the Bears (1961-1966). He played two years with Philadelphia and four years with the Dallas Cowboys before retiring after the 1972 season.
Ditka, who never hesitated to criticise a player, often had run-ins with his quarterbacks.

Ditka will be facing a daunting task in trying to turn around the Saints, one of the worst franchises since joining the league in 1967. The team did not record a winning record until 1987, when it posted a 12-3 mark.
The Saints are the only franchise in the NFL without a post-season victory, going 0-4 in the playoffs in their 30-year history.
New Orleans drew just 301,998 fans the past season, an average of 37,750 per game.
